problem: Copper(II) sulfate (CuSO₄) reacts with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to produce copper(II) hydroxide (Cu(OH)₂) and sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄). If 150.0 grams of CuSO₄ reacts completely, what mass of Cu(OH)₂ will be produced?
solution_steps: Calculate the molar mass of CuSO₄: 63.55 (Cu) + 32.07 (S) + 4 * 16.00 (O) = 159.62 g/mol.
Convert grams of CuSO₄ to moles: 150.0 g / 159.62 g/mol = 0.939 moles CuSO₄.
Write the balanced chemical equation: CuSO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Cu(OH)₂(s) + Na₂SO₄(aq).
Determine the mole ratio of Cu(OH)₂ to CuSO₄ from the balanced equation: 1 mole Cu(OH)₂ / 1 mole CuSO₄.
Calculate moles of Cu(OH)₂ produced: 0.939 moles CuSO₄ * (1 mole Cu(OH)₂ / 1 mole CuSO₄) = 0.939 moles Cu(OH)₂.
Calculate the molar mass of Cu(OH)₂: 63.55 (Cu) + 2 * (16.00 (O) + 1.01 (H)) = 97.62 g/mol.
Convert moles of Cu(OH)₂ to grams: 0.939 moles * 97.62 g/mol = 91.5 grams Cu(OH)₂.
